mode: image2image (vanilla CSFF card art as style reference)
prompt:
Use the attached reference images, each for one purpose.
Reference image 1 is the vanilla game's own map item (from Card Survival: Fantasy Forest): match its rendering style exactly and draw the map inside the frame the same way: a pale grey-cream parchment covered in thin dark ink lines for coasts and a river and many tiny tick marks for trees.
Reference image 2 is the COMPOSITION: keep this subject and layout (a map in a plain plank frame hung from a twine loop), redrawn in reference image 1's style.
Subject: a framed map: a hand-drawn parchment map of a coastline, a winding river and tiny tree tick marks, mounted in a plain narrow rectangular frame of four rough oak planks with square butt-joined corners, a loop of twine at the top for hanging, seen straight on with a slight tilt.
Style: flat posterized colour fills in a few tonal steps, cel-like, no soft gradients, no watercolour bleed, no paper texture; thin dark ink outlines and small ink hatch marks for wood grain; a muted naturalistic palette of grey-cream parchment, dull grey-brown wood and dark ink; realistic proportions; nothing glossy.
Single subject centred with a generous white margin on a solid flat pure white background (#FFFFFF) filling every edge, no ground shadow, no scenery. No text, no watermark, no signature, no border.
Avoid: watercolour, warm golden glow, sepia gradient, gilded ornate frame, glass glare, compass rose, readable lettering, sea monsters, wall, photo, 3D render, scenery behind the subject, grey background, off-white background, checkerboard.
note: Owner-approved 2026-10-10 in the Card Art Restyle Review (restyle toward vanilla card art). Finished by /process-card-art.
